score_notes.novelty: The HTML Popover API / top layer is a genuinely fresh web-platform mechanism the catalogue has not touched; pairing it with Lissitzky's slogan as a literal CSS-stacking demonstration is a new found-object + mechanism pairing only the web could do.
score_notes.nuance: Concept and execution collapse cleanly: the top layer's literal property (ignoring z-index) IS the slogan. Surface gag (red wedge beats whites) and literate reading (Constructivist propaganda as browser stacking) both land without wall text; restraint is good though not every element carries both readings (the Suprematist square is ballast, not load-bearing).
score_notes.narrative: Names Lissitzky and, behind him, Malevich; sits on the chance/order axis via per-visit rule-based Proun geometry; answers the catalogue's Malevich/Suprematist orbit and the 'browser chrome as material' thread (scrollbar-as-zip, favicon-as-Mondrian) with a mechanism none of them use.
score_notes.craft: Smallest build that completes the thought: one SVG generator, a stack of divs, one showPopover call; clean, no decoration, feature-detected fallback for older browsers.
score_notes.wit: The joke lands on the surface (red beats white) and again on re-reading (CSS stacking politics); the dry 'raise a white / affirm to the top layer' button copy carries the Constructivist register without overplaying it.

references_named: El Lissitzky, Beat the Whites with the Red Wedge (1919)
HTML Popover API / CSS top layer
rationale: A clean, well-built Lissitzky readymade that uses the HTML Popover API's top layer — a real, recent browser construct that ignores z-index — as the literal mechanism of the slogan. Concept and execution are the same object (P1), the per-visit rule-based Proun composition sits on the chance/order axis (P5), and the work extends the catalogue's browser-chrome-as-material thread with a mechanism none of the existing works use. Attribution, license, and ethics are all in order.
reservations: The Suprematist black square is decorative ballast rather than load-bearing; the work would be tighter without it. The 'Lower the whites' reset is a small convenience that slightly undercuts the irreversibility the slogan implies, though it is defensible as a Constructivist re-throw.
revision_suggestion: Consider dropping the black square (or making it functionally part of the wedge's escape) and letting 'Lower the whites' be a per-visit re-throw rather than a literal reset, so the Constructivist slogan stays fully irreversible.
